name: Brooklyn
intro: Brooklyn is New York City's most populous borough, known for its brownstone neighborhoods, waterfront districts, and strong local commercial corridors.
localFacts: ["Coextensive with Kings County and connected to Manhattan by the Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Williamsburg bridges", "Housing ranges from brownstone rowhouses in Park Slope and Bedford-Stuyvesant to high-rises in Downtown Brooklyn", "Served by more than a dozen subway lines plus the LIRR's Atlantic Terminal"]

name: Queens
intro: Queens is the largest NYC borough by area and one of the most ethnically diverse counties in the country, with major centers in Flushing, Jamaica, and Long Island City.
localFacts: ["Home to both JFK and LaGuardia airports", "Jamaica station is a major LIRR hub, and the 7 train links Flushing to Manhattan", "Housing stock mixes rowhouses, detached single-family homes, and large apartment complexes"]

name: Manhattan
intro: Manhattan is the commercial and cultural core of New York City, coextensive with New York County and dominated by apartment living.
localFacts: ["Anchored by the Midtown and Financial District business cores", "Grand Central Terminal and Penn Station are the region's principal commuter rail hubs", "Central Park spans 843 acres in the middle of the island"]

name: The Bronx
intro: The Bronx is the only New York City borough located primarily on the U.S. mainland, with dense residential neighborhoods and major parkland.
localFacts: ["Home to Yankee Stadium, the Bronx Zoo, and the New York Botanical Garden", "Served by numerous subway lines plus Metro-North's Harlem and Hudson lines", "The Grand Concourse is lined with one of the country's largest collections of Art Deco apartment buildings"]

name: Staten Island
intro: Staten Island is the least populous and most suburban NYC borough, linked to Brooklyn by the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and to Manhattan by ferry.
localFacts: ["The Staten Island Ferry provides free service between St. George and Lower Manhattan", "The Staten Island Railway runs the length of the borough from St. George to Tottenville", "Housing is largely single-family and townhouse construction, unusual for New York City"]

name: Hempstead
intro: The Town of Hempstead in southwestern Nassau County is the most populous town in New York State, encompassing dozens of villages and hamlets.
localFacts: ["Includes communities such as Levittown, Freeport, Valley Stream, and the Village of Hempstead", "Multiple LIRR branches, including the Babylon and Far Rockaway lines, cross the town", "Jones Beach State Park sits along the town's Atlantic barrier-island shore"]

name: North Hempstead
intro: The Town of North Hempstead covers northwestern Nassau County along the Long Island Sound shore, including Manhasset, Port Washington, Roslyn, and Great Neck.
localFacts: ["Occupies part of Long Island's Gold Coast, known for historic waterfront estates", "Served by the LIRR Port Washington Branch, a direct line to Penn Station with no transfer at Jamaica", "Housing is predominantly single-family, with village downtowns in Great Neck, Roslyn, and Port Washington"]

name: Oyster Bay
intro: The Town of Oyster Bay spans the full width of eastern Nassau County, from the Long Island Sound to the South Shore, including Hicksville, Bethpage, and Massapequa.
localFacts: ["The only Nassau town stretching from the North Shore to the South Shore", "Hicksville station is one of the busiest LIRR stops on Long Island", "Sagamore Hill, Theodore Roosevelt's home, is a National Historic Site in Oyster Bay hamlet"]

name: Glen Cove
intro: Glen Cove is one of Nassau County's two cities, located on the North Shore of Long Island overlooking Hempstead Harbor.
localFacts: ["One of only two cities in Nassau County, alongside Long Beach", "Sits on Long Island's Gold Coast, with several former estates now preserves and museums", "Served by the LIRR Oyster Bay Branch"]

name: Long Beach
intro: Long Beach is a city on a barrier island off Nassau County's South Shore, known for its oceanfront boardwalk and beach neighborhoods.
localFacts: ["Occupies a barrier island between the Atlantic Ocean and Reynolds Channel", "The LIRR Long Beach Branch terminates in the city, offering direct trains to Penn Station", "The oceanfront boardwalk stretches over two miles along the beach"]

name: Brookhaven
intro: The Town of Brookhaven is Suffolk County's most populous town, spanning the full width of central Long Island from the Sound to the Atlantic barrier beaches.
localFacts: ["Largest Suffolk town by population, including Patchogue, Stony Brook, Centereach, and Coram", "Home to Stony Brook University and Brookhaven National Laboratory", "The LIRR's Ronkonkoma and Port Jefferson branches serve the town, and ferries run from Port Jefferson to Connecticut"]

name: Islip
intro: The Town of Islip stretches along Suffolk County's South Shore and includes Bay Shore, Brentwood, and the county's main airport.
localFacts: ["Long Island MacArthur Airport in Ronkonkoma is within the town", "Ferries from Bay Shore serve Fire Island communities across the Great South Bay", "The LIRR Montauk and Ronkonkoma branches cross the town"]

name: Babylon
intro: The Town of Babylon occupies southwestern Suffolk County along the Great South Bay, including Lindenhurst, West Babylon, and Copiague.
localFacts: ["Babylon station is the terminus of the LIRR's electrified Babylon Branch", "Includes part of Jones Beach Island, with Cedar Beach and Gilgo Beach on the barrier island", "Housing is predominantly postwar suburban single-family neighborhoods"]

name: Huntington
intro: The Town of Huntington covers Suffolk County's northwestern corner on the Long Island Sound, with a well-known village downtown and harborside neighborhoods.
localFacts: ["Huntington village's downtown is a major North Shore dining and shopping district", "Huntington station is the end of LIRR electrification on the Port Jefferson Branch", "Melville, in the town's south, is a major Long Island office corridor along Route 110"]

name: Smithtown
intro: The Town of Smithtown sits on Suffolk County's North Shore between Huntington and Brookhaven, including Hauppauge, Kings Park, and St. James.
localFacts: ["The Hauppauge Industrial Park is one of the largest industrial parks in the Northeast", "The Nissequogue River runs through the town to the Long Island Sound", "Served by the LIRR Port Jefferson Branch, with stations at Smithtown, Kings Park, and St. James"]

name: Yonkers
intro: Yonkers is Westchester County's largest city, bordering the Bronx along the Hudson River with a redeveloping downtown waterfront.
localFacts: ["The fourth most populous city in New York State", "Metro-North's Hudson and Harlem lines both serve the city", "Its downtown waterfront along the Hudson has seen extensive residential redevelopment"]

name: Greenburgh
intro: The Town of Greenburgh in central Westchester includes the villages of Tarrytown, Dobbs Ferry, Hastings-on-Hudson, Irvington, Ardsley, and Elmsford plus unincorporated areas like Hartsdale.
localFacts: ["Its Hudson River villages are known as the Rivertowns", "Metro-North's Hudson and Harlem lines serve opposite sides of the town", "The Mario M. Cuomo Bridge lands at Tarrytown, linking Westchester to Rockland County"]

name: New Rochelle
intro: New Rochelle is a city on the Long Island Sound in southern Westchester, with a high-rise downtown undergoing major transit-oriented redevelopment.
localFacts: ["Sits on the Long Island Sound with a large city park on Glen Island", "Metro-North's New Haven Line provides a roughly half-hour ride to Grand Central", "Downtown has added significant high-rise residential development around the train station"]

name: Mount Vernon
intro: Mount Vernon is a compact, densely populated city directly north of the Bronx in southern Westchester County.
localFacts: ["One of the most densely populated cities in New York State, in just over four square miles", "Served by Metro-North's Harlem and New Haven lines at Mount Vernon West and Mount Vernon East", "Borders the Bronx, with many residents commuting into the city by rail and subway connections"]

name: White Plains
intro: White Plains is the county seat and commercial hub of Westchester County, with a high-rise downtown of offices, retail, and apartments.
localFacts: ["County seat of Westchester County and home to its government center and courts", "A major stop on Metro-North's Harlem Line, roughly 35 minutes from Grand Central", "Downtown functions as Westchester's principal office and shopping district"]

name: Ramapo
intro: The Town of Ramapo is Rockland County's most populous town, in the county's southwest along the New Jersey border, including Suffern, Monsey, and Spring Valley.
localFacts: ["The most populous town in Rockland County", "Includes the villages of Suffern, Spring Valley (in part), Airmont, and New Square", "The Ramapo Mountains and Harriman State Park lands rise along the town's edge"]

name: Clarkstown
intro: The Town of Clarkstown occupies central Rockland County and includes New City, the county seat, along with Nanuet and Congers.
localFacts: ["New City, the Rockland County seat, is within the town", "The Palisades Center in West Nyack is one of the largest shopping malls in the country", "Rockland Lake State Park sits along the town's Hudson River side"]

name: Orangetown
intro: The Town of Orangetown covers Rockland County's southeastern corner along the Hudson River and New Jersey border, including Nyack, Pearl River, and Orangeburg.
localFacts: ["The village of Nyack is a well-known Hudson riverfront downtown near the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge", "Borders New Jersey, with Pearl River on the Pascack Valley commuter rail line", "Hook Mountain and Nyack Beach state parks line the Hudson shore"]

name: Haverstraw
intro: The Town of Haverstraw sits on the Hudson River in northern Rockland County, including the villages of Haverstraw and West Haverstraw.
localFacts: ["The Hudson River reaches its widest point, Haverstraw Bay, along the town's shore", "The riverfront village of Haverstraw was historically a major brickmaking center", "High Tor and part of Harriman State Park rise behind the riverfront"]

name: Stony Point
intro: The Town of Stony Point is Rockland County's northernmost town, a largely residential community on the west bank of the Hudson River.
localFacts: ["Stony Point Battlefield, site of a 1779 Revolutionary War battle, is a state historic site on the Hudson", "Bear Mountain and Harriman state park lands cover much of the town's western area", "The northernmost and least populous of Rockland's five towns"]

name: Ithaca
intro: Ithaca is the Tompkins County seat at the southern end of Cayuga Lake, a college city shaped by Cornell University and Ithaca College and by the gorges that cut through its hillsides.
localFacts: ["Home to Cornell University, whose campus overlooks the city from East Hill", "Ithaca College sits on South Hill overlooking the city and Cayuga Lake", "Gorges and waterfalls, including Ithaca Falls, run through the city to Cayuga Lake"]

name: Dryden
intro: Dryden is a village and surrounding town in eastern Tompkins County on the Route 13 corridor between Ithaca and Cortland, mixing a small village center with rural hamlets like Varna and Etna.
localFacts: ["The main campus of Tompkins Cortland Community College is in the village", "Route 13 links the village to Ithaca and Cortland", "The surrounding Town of Dryden is one of Tompkins County's largest municipalities by area"]

name: Lansing
intro: The Town of Lansing stretches along the east shore of Cayuga Lake north of Ithaca, mixing lakeshore homes, farmland, and newer residential development.
localFacts: ["Runs along the east shore of Cayuga Lake directly north of Ithaca", "Includes the separately incorporated Village of Lansing near the Ithaca border", "Myers Park on Cayuga Lake is the town's well-known lakefront park"]

name: Groton
intro: The Town of Groton occupies the northeastern corner of Tompkins County, centered on the Village of Groton amid rolling farmland.
localFacts: ["The Village of Groton is the town's population and commercial center", "Sits in the county's northeast corner near the Cortland and Cayuga county lines", "Route 222 connects the village east toward Cortland"]

name: Newfield
intro: The Town of Newfield lies southwest of Ithaca along Route 13, a rural town of wooded hills, farms, and state forest land.
localFacts: ["The Newfield Covered Bridge, built in 1853, is one of the oldest covered bridges still in use in New York", "Route 13 links the hamlet of Newfield to Ithaca", "Large tracts of state forest cover the town's hills"]

name: Margaretville
intro: Margaretville is a village on the East Branch of the Delaware River in the western Catskills, serving as the commercial hub of Delaware County's Route 28 corridor.
localFacts: ["Sits on the East Branch of the Delaware River along Route 28", "Serves as a commercial center for the surrounding western Catskills communities", "The Belleayre Mountain ski center is a short drive east on Route 28"]

name: Fleischmanns
intro: Fleischmanns is a small village in eastern Delaware County on Route 28, a onetime Catskills resort town named for the Fleischmann yeast family who summered there.
localFacts: ["Named for the Fleischmann family of yeast fame, who kept a summer compound here", "Sits along Route 28 near the Ulster County line", "A short drive from the Belleayre Mountain ski center"]

name: Andes
intro: Andes is a hilltop town in the central Catskills of Delaware County, with a small hamlet center known for antiques shops and its setting near the Pepacton Reservoir.
localFacts: ["The Pepacton Reservoir, part of the New York City water supply, borders the town", "The hamlet's Main Street is known for antiques shops and galleries", "Site of an 1845 confrontation in New York's Anti-Rent War"]

name: Roxbury
intro: The Town of Roxbury lies in the northeastern corner of Delaware County along the East Branch of the Delaware River, including the hamlets of Roxbury and Grand Gorge.
localFacts: ["The Catskill Scenic Trail, a rail-trail on the former Ulster & Delaware line, runs through the town", "Birthplace of naturalist John Burroughs and railroad financier Jay Gould", "Includes the hamlets of Roxbury and Grand Gorge along Route 30"]

name: Arkville
intro: Arkville is a hamlet on Route 28 between Margaretville and Fleischmanns in the western Catskills, in the Town of Middletown.
localFacts: ["Home base of the Delaware & Ulster Railroad excursion line", "Sits on Route 28 between Margaretville and Fleischmanns", "The Catskill Center for Conservation and Development is headquartered here"]
